rationale: The abstract describes original research developing four machine‑learning models (including SVM, random forest, neural network) to predict heart‑failure readmission and reports an AUC of 0.602, indicating a quantitative performance metric for an adult HF cohort.

The abstract describes original development of several machine‑learning models (random forests, boosting, etc.) to predict 30‑ and 180‑day readmission in heart‑failure patients, reporting C‑statistics as performance metrics.

The study develops a multi‑layer perceptron machine‑learning model to predict 30‑day heart‑failure readmission or death in adults (≥65 y) and reports performance metrics (AUC, AUPRC, sensitivity, specificity), meeting all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

The abstract describes original research developing machine‑learning models (tree‑augmented naive Bayes, random forest, gradient‑boosted) to predict 30‑day readmission in adult heart‑failure patients and reports C‑statistics as performance metrics, satisfying all inclusion criteria.

The study develops and validates a machine‑learning (CatBoost) model for adult heart‑failure patients, predicting 30‑day and 1‑year HF readmission or all‑cause mortality, and reports AUC‑ROC performance metrics (e.g., 74.16‑85.73).
The article develops a deep learning (DUNs) model to predict 30‑day readmission in adult heart‑failure patients and reports performance metrics (AUC 0.705, accuracy 76.4%).

The abstract describes original research developing six supervised machine‑learning models to predict in‑hospital all‑cause mortality in adult heart‑failure patients, and reports performance metrics (AUCs 0.62‑0.82, accuracies up to 88%).

The abstract describes original research developing ML algorithms to predict all‑cause mortality in hospitalized adult heart‑failure patients and reports AUC performance metrics, meeting all inclusion criteria.

The study develops a deep‑learning model for HF patients (adult) and evaluates a Cox model predicting all‑cause mortality and rehospitalisation, reporting AUC 0.93 and C‑index 0.71, thus meeting all inclusion criteria.

The abstract describes original research developing multiple machine‑learning models to predict hospitalization (a readmission outcome) in heart‑failure patients and reports quantitative performance metrics (accuracy, PPV, NPV).

The study develops a deep‑learning model using adult heart‑failure patients and reports performance (AUC 0.613) for predicting 30‑day all‑cause readmission or death, meeting all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.
The title indicates a machine‑learning frailty index for heart‑failure patients but does not mention hospital readmission, mortality outcomes, or provide any quantitative performance metrics.

The abstract describes using machine learning to predict readmission or death in heart failure but does not present any quantitative performance metric (e.g., AUC, accuracy) required by inclusion criterion I4.
The source is a conference abstract that does not present full primary data and the abstract provides no quantitative performance metric (e.g., AUC) for the machine‑learning model.

The title indicates a machine‑learning model for mortality prediction in heart patients, but the abstract is unavailable and no quantitative performance metric (e.g., AUC) is reported, violating the requirement for a performance measure.

The abstract describes original research developing machine‑learning models (decision trees, ANN, SVM) to predict 1‑month and 3‑month readmission in heart‑failure patients and reports performance metrics such as AUC and accuracy.

The abstract describes original research developing four machine‑learning models to predict all‑cause rehospitalisation and death in adult patients after a first heart‑failure admission, and reports performance metrics (AUC, sensitivity, specificity).

The abstract describes development of ML models for 3‑year all‑cause mortality but does not report any quantitative performance metric such as AUC, accuracy, or calibration; only hazard ratios are provided.

The abstract reports original development of machine‑learning models (random forests, GBM) in 9502 adult heart‑failure patients, evaluating all‑cause mortality and HF hospitalization with quantitative metrics (C‑statistics, AUPRC, Brier scores).

The study develops machine‑learning models (Random Forest, Gradient Boosting) for predicting death in adult heart‑failure patients and reports performance metrics such as c‑index 0.714 and balanced accuracy 0.74, satisfying all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

The study develops and compares six machine‑learning models to predict hospital readmission in a retrospective cohort of 1,856 adult heart‑failure patients and reports performance metrics such as accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity.

The study develops and evaluates multiple machine‑learning models to predict in‑hospital mortality in adult heart‑failure patients, reporting AUC values (e.g., 0.882) and calibration metrics, thus meeting all inclusion criteria.

The abstract describes original research developing a random‑forest machine‑learning model to predict 1‑year all‑cause and HF‑specific readmission in adult heart‑failure patients, reporting C‑statistics of 0.68 and 0.69 as performance metrics.

The abstract describes original research developing and validating machine‑learning models (random forests, XGBoost, LightGBM) in 4,904 adult heart‑failure patients to predict 180‑day mortality or emergency hospitalization, and reports performance metrics such as area under the precision‑recall curve, calibration slope and Brier score.

The study develops machine‑learning models (e.g., SVM, Gradient Boosting) to predict heart‑failure survival, mortality, and 30‑day readmission in adult patients, reporting quantitative performance metrics such as 88.41% accuracy and ROC‑AUC scores.

The title indicates a risk‑factor analysis of readmission/early death in a telemonitoring program, with no indication that a machine‑learning or deep‑learning model was developed or evaluated, nor any quantitative performance metric reported.

The study develops and validates an AI‑based (MLP/Transformer) prediction model for all‑cause mortality in adult heart‑failure patients and reports performance metrics such as C‑index (0.801). It meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

The abstract describes original research developing machine‑learning models (random forest, SVM, gradient boosting) to predict all‑cause mortality in adult heart‑failure patients (mean age 51) and reports quantitative performance (AUC up to 0.926), meeting all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusions.

The title suggests a machine‑learning model predicting heart‑failure readmissions, but the abstract is unavailable and no quantitative performance metric is reported, violating the requirement for a performance measure.

The study develops a deep learning model for predicting all‑cause mortality in heart‑failure patients (30‑day, 180‑day, 365‑day outcomes) using the adult MIMIC‑III cohort and reports performance metrics such as AUC (e.g., micro‑average AUC 91%).

The abstract describes original research developing multiple machine‑learning classifiers to predict 20‑day hospital readmission in heart‑failure patients, reports adult HF population, and provides performance metrics (AUC, sensitivity, specificity).

The study develops a machine‑learning prognostic algorithm for adult heart‑failure patients (mean age 68) to predict rehospitalisation, reporting quantitative performance (76‑88% sensitivity, 85% specificity).

The study develops multiple machine‑learning models to predict in‑hospital and 6‑month mortality and 30‑day/90‑day readmission in adult heart‑failure patients, reporting performance metrics such as AUC, accuracy, sensitivity and specificity.

The study develops machine‑learning prediction models for 28‑day all‑cause mortality in adult patients (age > 18) with pre‑existing chronic heart failure and reports quantitative performance (AUC 0.801), meeting all inclusion criteria.

The abstract describes original development and external validation of ML/DL models (ResNet, CatBoost) predicting 1‑, 3‑, and 5‑year all‑cause mortality in adult heart‑failure patients, and reports AUROC performance metrics (85%‑92% internal, 78%‑82% external).
The study develops an XGBoost machine‑learning model to predict all‑cause mortality in adult heart failure patients and reports quantitative performance metrics (AUC = 0.83, accuracy = 81.58%).

The deep‑learning model predicts LV global longitudinal strain (LVGLS) from ECG, a diagnostic measure, and its performance metrics (AUROC 0.82–0.85) relate to LVGLS, not directly to hospital readmission or mortality. The study does not develop a model whose primary outcome is readmission or mortality.

The abstract reports a retrospective cohort study that develops an XGBoost machine‑learning model to predict in‑hospital mortality in adult ICU patients with heart failure, providing an AUC of 0.824 and comparing it with other ML models.

The abstract describes development of ensemble machine‑learning models to predict readmission in a large adult heart‑failure cohort, reporting quantitative performance metrics (AUC = 0.70, F1‑score = 0.58).

The study reports original research developing eight machine‑learning models for predicting in‑hospital mortality in adult heart‑failure patients (≥65 years) and reports quantitative performance metrics (AUC = 0.850, accuracy = 0.738, etc.).
The abstract describes a use‑case for a CDS tool but does not report any quantitative performance metric (e.g., AUC, sensitivity, specificity) for the model, violating inclusion criterion I4.

The abstract describes development of three predictive models combining structured data and natural language processing for heart‑failure readmission, reporting AUCs (0.6494, 0.6447, 0.5219) as quantitative performance metrics.

The study reports an original machine‑learning model developed for adult patients with ischemic cardiomyopathy and HFpEF, predicts major adverse cardiovascular events including cardiac mortality (meeting I3), and reports quantitative performance (C‑index 0.768/0.633) (meeting I4).
The abstract reports development of decision‑tree machine‑learning models for 1‑year worsening HF hospitalization and all‑cause death in adults with incident HFrEF, providing AUC performance metrics.
The abstract reports development of machine‑learning prognostic models for all‑cause mortality and HF hospitalization in adults with HFpEF, providing C‑index performance metrics.

The study develops and externally validates a random forest machine‑learning model to predict in‑hospital mortality in adults with heart failure, reporting quantitative performance metrics (c‑statistic 0.96, sensitivity 87.3%, specificity 90.6%).
The abstract reports a machine‑learning model developed on adult Takotsubo cardiomyopathy patients (≥18 years) to predict in‑hospital mortality, with AUC performance metrics provided.

The abstract reports development and external validation of a CatBoost machine‑learning model for predicting hospital mortality in mechanically ventilated patients with congestive heart failure, providing AUC values (0.833, 0.806) as quantitative performance metrics.

The study reports original research developing multimodal machine‑learning models for adult heart‑failure patients, predicting 30‑day all‑cause mortality and hospital readmission, and reports quantitative performance metrics (AUC 0.881 for mortality, 0.709 for readmission).
The study reports original research developing machine‑learning models (GBM, RF, EN) to predict 30‑day readmission and death in heart failure patients, providing quantitative AUC performance metrics.
The abstract does not provide any age information for the 7696 patients, so there is no evidence that the study population consists of adults (≥18 years).

The study develops machine‑learning models (e.g., XGBoost) for adult chronic heart failure patients and reports quantitative performance metrics (AUC 0.754 for death, 0.718 for HF rehospitalization) for prognostic outcomes such as mortality and readmission.

The study reports a deep‑learning model developed on adult heart‑failure patients and reports a C‑statistic of 0.91 for predicting 1‑year all‑cause death or severe progression, satisfying all inclusion criteria.

The study develops a deep‑learning survival prediction model (DLSPCXR/DLSPinteg) for adult heart failure patients and reports quantitative performance metrics (AUC 0.757–0.826) for mortality prediction.

The abstract reports a deep‑learning model developed for predicting rehospitalization in adults with acute heart failure, providing AUC values (0.63–0.76) for 30‑, 90‑, and 365‑day readmission, satisfying all inclusion criteria.

The study develops a linear discriminant analysis (LDA) machine‑learning model to predict 28‑day all‑cause mortality in adult heart failure patients in the ICU, reporting quantitative performance metrics such as AUC and accuracy.
